### Boundedness (Real Numbers)

:::{.definition data-title="Bounded Real Sets"}

A set $A \subset \mathbb{R}$ of real numbers is **bounded from above** if there
exists a real number $M \in \mathbb{R}$, called an **upper bound** of $A$ such
that $x \leq M$ for all $x \in A$. Similarly, $A$ is **bounded from below** if
there exists a real number $m \in \mathbb{R}$, called a **lower bound** of $A$
such that $x \geq m$ for all $x \in A$. Furthermore, we say a set $A$ is
**bounded** if it is bounded both from above and below.

:::

Equivalently, a set $A$ is bounded if $A \subset I$ for some bounded interval
$I=[m,M]$.
